title: AdicFiniteReductionTor
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring and $J$ an ideal. Use constant coefficient sheaves, module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The normalized constructions are [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. For $N$ in the pro-etale derived category put $P_n=A/J^{n+1}$ and $N_n=N\otimes_A^L P_n$, and let $\nu^*$ be the recorded comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $C$ be a bounded constructible etale $P_0$-complex [def-pe-etale-constructible-module], and let $e:\nu^*C\simeq N_0$. If $a\le b$ and $C$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], then every $N_n$ has pro-etale Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. No completeness of $N$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use coefficientModelTorAmplitude_iff_flatModel to represent C by a complex of flat sheaves supported in [a,b]. Bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat. The normalized ordinary inverse image in AdicFiniteReductionData preserves flat terms, K-flatness and zero terms, and its specified derived comparison is invertible on this model. The bounded flat criterion on the pro-etale model transfers the Tor interval to the normalized pullback and then through e to N_0. This preservation argument does not need constructibility, compactness, quasi-separatedness, or the finite-Tor comparison equivalence.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative P of N using exists_coefficientModelFlatKFlatRepresentative. Its ordinary scalar extensions P_n along A -> A/J^(n+1) are K-flat. The existing universal derived scalar-extension comparisons identify Q(P_n) with the actual normalized reductions. For a coefficient map f and module M over its target, balanced tensor cancellation gives Res_f(M tensor E_f(P)) isomorphic to Res_f(M) tensor P, naturally in every term and differential. Symmetry and the single-complex tensor isomorphisms identify this with the two coefficientModelTensorTest complexes. Exact faithful restriction of scalars preserves and reflects vanishing in every degree.

proof.text: Choose finitely many generators of J. The constant quotient surjectivity and kernel formula from flat_and_quotients identify the sectionwise residue kernel with the ideal generated by their constant global sections. A module over A/J^(n+1), restricted to the A coefficient sheaf, is killed by the (n+1)-st power of this ideal: map ideals through each constant-section ring homomorphism, commute ideal maps with powers, and use the kernel formula for the nth quotient. Pass from sectionwise annihilation to annihilation by the ideal of global scalar endomorphisms using evaluation on every object.

proof.text: For a fixed q outside [a,b], balance the residue bound to obtain vanishing of the P tensor test on every restricted residue module. Prove vanishing for modules killed by the m-th power of the finitely generated global ideal by induction on m. For m=0 the identity is zero. At the successor step use the existing finite image/cokernel filtration in exists_shortExact_of_smul_eq_zero_of_mem_pow_succ. Its submodule is killed by the previous power. Its quotient is killed by every generator and hence by the sectionwise residue kernel; the proved exists_quotient_module helper from NilpotentCoefficientTensorAcyclic equips it with its unique quotient-ring action. The base tensor vanishing thus applies to this quotient. Fixed K-flat tensor is triangulated, and its representative comparison identifies these tensor tests with derived tensor of degree-zero modules. The exact middle segment of the derived homology sequence and induction give the required vanishing. Apply this at m=n+1, balance back to P_n, and transport to every K-flat representative by coefficientModelTensorTest_iso. Exponent zero, an empty generating family, J=0, J=A, and the zero ring are covered by the same argument.

theorem adicFiniteReduction_tor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (N : adicFiniteAmbient.{u, v} X A)
    (C : adicFiniteEtale.{u, v} X J 0)
    (hC : IsCoefficientBoundedConstructibleEtale.{u, v} X (adicFiniteCoeff J 0) C)
    (e : (adicFinitePullback.{u, v} X (adicFiniteCoeff J 0)).obj C ≅
      adicFiniteReduction.{u, v} X J N 0)
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hTor : HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude
      (constant (smallModelComparisonEtaleTopology.{u, v} X) (adicFiniteCoeff J 0)) C a b) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, HasCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude.{u, v} X (adicFiniteCoeff J n)
      (adicFiniteReduction.{u, v} X J N n) a b
